sentences.text: Aleosteus was an extinct genus of arthrodire placoderm fish that lived during the Early Devonian period.
Fossils include almost complete juvenile and adult specimens characterized by a short, broad skull that is concave at the back.
The type species Aleosteus eganensis was described in 2000 from fossils found in the Late Emsian strata of the Sevy Dolomite Formation in the Egan Range of east-central Nevada, USA.
The species name eganensis is derived from the Egan Mountain Range where the type locality is located.
Aleosteus is considered a basal member of the order Arthrodira and is closely related to the genus Simblaspis.
The genus belongs to the family Actinolepididae.
Aleosteus lived between 399.5 and 393.47 million years ago during the Emsian stage.
